title: Business cycle
competency: Describe the business cycle and its four phases.

keywords.def: Economy-wide ups and downs in production, trade and activity around a long-term growth trend.
The phase when employment and output rise and prices face upward pressure.
The highest point of the cycle: maximum output, full employment, inflation pressure.
The phase when growth slows, unemployment rises and price pressure eases.
The lowest point of the cycle, from which the next expansion starts.

ideas.name: The business cycle and its phases

en.text: The business (trade) cycle is the economy-wide rise and fall of production, trade and activity around a long-term growth trend. It has four phases: expansion (employment and output rise, prices face upward pressure), peak (maximum output, full employment, inflation pressure), contraction (growth slows, unemployment rises) and trough (the lowest point). Cycles recur but are irregular, and governments try to manage them with policy, as Egypt manages the Nile with the Aswan Dam.

screens.title: Up and down
screens.ask: Output grows over many years, but not smoothly. What usually happens in the short run?
opts: It rises and falls around a rising trend
It rises by exactly the same amount every year
screens.after: Booms and slumps repeat around the long-term growth trend (Figure 1.1).

screens.title: The business cycle
paras: Also called the trade cycle, economic cycle or boom-bust cycle.
It is the economy-wide ups and downs in production, trade and economic activity.
GDP expands and contracts around a long-term growth trend.
Every boom is followed by a slump, and vice versa (Vaish, 2010).
Cycles recur, but their length and depth are irregular and hard to predict.

paras: Figure 1.1: output wave around a rising trend line.

growth slows, unemployment rises, price pressure eases
lowest point; the next expansion starts

screens.title: Can it be controlled?
paras: Economists use models: simplified frameworks of the economy.
They ask what causes fluctuations and how to avoid recessions.
Egypt controls the Nile floods with the Aswan Dam.
Likewise, society tries to control the cycle with economic policy (Mankiw, 2016).

screens.title: Put the phases in order, starting from a trough
screens.why: Trough → expansion → peak → contraction → next trough.
screens.clue: After the lowest point, the economy grows.

screens.title: Match each phase to a sign
screens.clue: Peak and trough are points; the others are movements.

screens.title: Expansion or contraction?
screens.why: Expansion: more output, jobs and price pressure. Contraction: the reverse.

screens.text: Business cycles are perfectly regular, so recessions can be predicted exactly.
screens.why: p.15: "Recessions are common but irregular." Cycles recur but their timing and depth vary.

screens.text: In Figure 1.1 the second trough is higher than the first. Why?
opts: The cycle moves around a rising growth trend
screens.ans: The cycle moves around a rising growth trend
screens.why: Peaks and troughs both trend upward because long-run growth continues.
screens.clue: Look at the dashed trend line.

screens.text: At a peak, which problem worries policy makers most, according to the book's description?
screens.why: At the peak output is at its maximum and employment is full, so "inflationary pressures on prices are evident".
screens.clue: What happens to prices when demand is highest?
